en: The Questions of Milinda,
Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena,
Section 5: The Question of the Equal Status of Two Beings Born in the World.
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, between one who dies here and is reborn in the Brahma-world, and one who dies here and is reborn in Kaśmīra, which is the longer and which is the swifter?
"They are equal, O Great King," he replied.
“Make a simile,” [the king said].
“But where, great king, is your birthplace?
“There is, venerable sir, a village named Kalasi; there I was born.”
“How far away, Great King, is the village of Kalasi from here?
“About two hundred yojanas, Bhante.
“How far away, Great King, is Kaśmīra from here?”
“Twelve leagues, venerable sir.
“Well then, Great King, consider Kalaṃsi Village.
“It has been considered, venerable sir.”
“Come now, Great King, consider Kaśmīra.
“It has been considered, Bhante.
“Which, Great King, was considered more slowly, and which more quickly?”
“It is equal, Bhante.
“In the same way, Great King, one who dies here and is reborn in the Brahma-world, and one who dies here and is reborn in Kashmir, are reborn equally.
“Give me a further simile.”
“What do you think, great king? Suppose two birds were flying through the air; one were to alight on a tall tree and the other on a short tree.
When they have both settled at the same time, whose shadow would fall upon the earth first, and whose shadow would take longer to reach the earth?”
“It is equal, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, one who dies here and is reborn in the Brahma-world, and one who dies here and is reborn in Kashmir, are reborn at exactly the same time.
“Well said, venerable Nāgasena!”
The fifth question: On the state of equality between two things arisen in the world.
